concept.name: Rolling-window analysis
concept.definition: Walk-forward analysis whose training window has fixed length and drops the oldest observations as it advances.
concept.intuition: It estimates how a fitted choice behaves on observations that were not used to fit that choice.
concept.mechanics: Choose train and test lengths, fit on each trailing window, and evaluate on the immediately following block.
concept.failure_modes: Random splitting, overlapping labels, repeated tuning, or an unprotected final test set can produce optimistic estimates.
concept.misconceptions: Validation measures conditional generalization under a split design; it does not guarantee future market performance.
concept.example: Use the prior 36 months to fit each model and predict the next month, then roll both boundaries forward one month.
